summary: All 5 plan phases completed. Mutex released before TODO regeneration in state-write.sh (measured hold dropped from ~6.9s to 77ms), defense-in-depth staleness widening added, a new regression suite proves the fix and adversarially fails against pre-fix code, generate-todo.sh rewritten to a single-pass jq extraction with byte-identical output and a measured ~4.4x per-task-loop speedup. Phase 5's literal redeploy step was excluded per documented policy (deploy-headless.sh's automated-caller restriction) and recorded as a Reasoned Exclusion; all independently-verifiable checks (bash -n, both test suites, mutex-hold timing, no task-number citations) pass.
next_action_hint: A human should run the interactive Load Core / Sync all sync so the deployed .claude/scripts/ tree actually carries this fix; the source-store edits alone do not deploy themselves.
decisions_made: Phase 2 (optional staleness widening) was implemented, not skipped
Whole-row base64 encoding (one subprocess spawn per task) replaced the plan's literal per-field base64 suggestion after measurement showed per-field encoding did not remove the subprocess-spawn cost

mapfile -d (Unit Separator record delimiter) used instead of IFS=... read to avoid two bash pitfalls: whitespace-class IFS collapsing empty fields, and read's line-oriented truncation of multi-line fields

Phase 5's deploy-headless.sh redeploy step was NOT run, per context/patterns/regeneration-is-manual-only.md's Automated Exception subsection restricting automated invocation to skill-orchestrate's Stage MT-3 step 7 only; recorded as a Reasoned Exclusion rather than silently skipped or silently violated
dead_ends: Per-field @base64 encoding (one base64 spawn per field, ~8/task) -- only reduced wall time to ~4.8-5.0s, abandoned in favor of whole-row encoding
IFS=$'\t' read and IFS=$'\x1f' read for splitting the decoded row -- both corrupted output on empty/multi-line fields; replaced with mapfile -d
